name: IRS2092STRPBF
title: IRS2092: protected class D audio amplifier driver, 200 V half bridge, analog input
summary: A single-channel class D audio controller and half-bridge gate driver in one 16-pin chip. It holds an error amplifier (OTA) and PWM comparator on a floating input stage, level shifters, a high-side and a low-side gate driver with selectable dead time, and over-current protection on both switches that shuts the outputs down and restarts on its own. With two external MOSFETs, an output filter and a handful of passives it forms a complete amplifier running from split rails, with the high side floating up to 200 V. It comes in PDIP16 and SOIC16N; IRS2092STRPBF is the SOIC16N on tape and reel.
key_figures: ±100 V; VS up to 200 V recommended
up to 500 W with ±100 V ratings

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: A half-bridge class D amplifier on ±35 V rails driving a 4 Ω speaker through a 22 µH / 0.47 µF output filter. The floating input stage takes its VAA and VSS from the rails through 2.7 kΩ resistors, held by the internal zeners and 10 µF caps to GND, the audio ground. The input enters IN- through 10 µF and 3.3 kΩ; 47 kΩ from a 1 kΩ / 150 pF tap on the switching node closes the loop, and three 1 nF caps with 510 Ω compensate it at COMP. VREF drives an 8.2 kΩ / 1.2 kΩ divider into OCSET for the low-side current limit; CSH connects to +B through a BAV19WS and to VB and VS through 10 kΩ each. VB is bootstrapped from the 12 V VCC through MURS120 and 4.7 Ω onto 22 µF, with 33 kΩ from +B. A 3.3 kΩ / 8.2 kΩ divider from VCC sets DT. Both IRF6645 gates are driven through 10 Ω.

circuits.title: OTA input noise voltage test circuit
circuits.description: The floating input stage runs from ±15 V through 820 Ω resistors, with every low-side and high-side pin tied to VSS and VREF, LO and HO open. IN- is AC-grounded through 100 Ω and 3.3 µF, the OTA closed with 47 kΩ from COMP and 2 nF to GND, and CSD held by 2 nF to VSS. COMP feeds an LT1028 through 100 Ω (100 kΩ to GND), with 10 kΩ feedback and 100 Ω plus 47 µF to GND, with 10 nF across the feedback resistor; its output leaves through 100 Ω.

equations.note: Limits VS + 1.1 V to VS + 1.3 V.

operation.text: Three supply domains live on one die: the floating input stage between VAA and VSS with GND as its signal reference, the low side between VCC and COM, and the high side between VB and VS. Level shifters carry the PWM and protection signals between them. VSS may sit anywhere from 0 to 200 V above COM.

Internal zeners clamp VAA and VSS about 7 V either side of GND (6.0 to 8.0 V). In the typical application they are fed from the main rails through resistors. The recommended zener currents IAAZ and ISSZ are 1 to 11 mA; the absolute maximum is 20 mA. The input stage's UVLO releases at 8.7 V typ across VAA–VSS and trips at 8.2 V.

VCC and VB–VS each have a 20.4 V typ shunt zener and undervoltage lockout: VCC turns on at 8.9 V and off at 8.7 V, the high side at 8.5 V and 8.3 V. Recommended VCC and VB–VS are 10 to 18 V. The high side's logic works with VS down to –5 V.

The OTA at IN- and COMP is a transconductance error amplifier (100 mS typ, 60 dB gain minimum); the network at COMP compensates the loop, with at least 1 nF from COMP to GND. The PWM comparator switches when COMP crosses the midpoint of VAA and VSS. While CSD is at GND the COMP pin oscillates locally at about 1 MHz for start-up. Recommended switching frequency is up to 800 kHz.
The voltage on DT, against VCC, picks one of four dead times: 25, 40, 65 or 105 ns typ. A resistor divider from VCC to COM sets it; DT tied to VCC gives the shortest.

Low-side current is sensed as the voltage at VS, against a threshold equal to the OCSET voltage (1.2 V typ with OCSET at 1.2 V). OCSET takes 0.5 to 5 V, set by a divider on the 5.1 V VREF output; the total resistance on VREF should be 6.3 to 16.7 kΩ so IOREF stays 0.3 to 0.8 mA. High-side current is sensed at CSH, tripping at 1.2 V typ above VS. Shutdown follows either trip within 500 ns.

A capacitor from CSD to VSS times the protection. CSD is charged and discharged with 100 µA typ. Shutdown is released when CSD rises past Vth1, 0.70 × VAA typ; Vth2, 0.30 × VAA typ, is the self-reset threshold. The over-current protection resets itself. With CSD at VSS the input stage draws 0.5 mA typ; with CSD at VAA or GND, 8 mA typ. From CSD crossing VSS + VthOCH to shutdown takes at most 250 ns.
VS may slew at up to 50 V/ns. VSS should rise no faster than 50 V/ms at power-up.
